messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — a customer on Dedicated reported that after a recent RBAC change their SIEM shows audit events with missing 'actor' and truncated 'resource.path'. Can we checklist what could cause this (webhook vs S3 path)?
priya: Hmm. Two quick suspects: 1) our event sanitizer step that redacts PII might be over-eager for that tenant due to a policy tag, 2) truncation could happen on the delivery side (Splunk HEC or webhook proxy). Do we have a sample payload?
sam: Customer attached a webhook sample. Posting redacted snippet: ```json
{
  "event_type": "permission.change",
  "actor": null,
  "resource": { "path": "/org/very/long/resource/name/that/keeps/going/and/is/longer/than/expected..." },
  "meta": { "tenant_id": "acct-78" }
}\```
lex: Noted. If actor is null that could be from our RBAC migration that switches to subject IDs vs emails — if we didn't populate subject_email for that tenant, downstream mapping will show null. Truncation for resource.path looks like Splunk HEC default max_event_len (config on collector) or a proxy that limits header/body size. Which delivery mechanism is this customer using?
maya: They're using webhook delivery to a Splunk HEC endpoint (via partner proxy), but they also want an S3 fallback. They enabled SSE-KMS for S3. Any KMS interplay we should verify?
priya: For SSE-KMS S3 exports we add x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms and include key-id on the bucket policy. Important: when we upload gzip batches, we set metadata headers; if the partner's S3 ingestion pipeline strips metadata or re-encrypts, you can lose the original content-type info which might make downstream parsers treat payload as text and truncate. Also ensure our signed webhook HMAC header isn't being dropped by the proxy — that can affect validation steps for onboarding.
sam: For Splunk specifically, ask them to check props/transforms on the collector. Default HEC has max_event_size and max_content_length. We've seen truncation around 64k where long resource paths get chopped. Suggest they increase max_event_size or store the full resource in a separate field (resource.full_path) on our side for large names.
lex: Actionable onboarding checklist I propose: 1) send canonical sample events (we'll provide) 2) ask customer to capture raw request at their ingress (verify headers intact) 3) if webhook -> confirm proxy/collector max sizes 4) if S3 -> confirm SSE-KMS key policy and that object metadata is preserved 5) run our contract test harness (POST -> their endpoint with HMAC verification)
priya: I'll add a short contract test we can give them. Example curl (they should replace X-SIG and URL):
```bash
curl -X POST https://customer-collector.example.com/hec -H 'Authorization: Splunk 012345:abcdef' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Redwood-HMAC: sha256=...' --data-binary @sample_event.json
```
maya: Nice. Also, is there an audit schema change we need to flag? We shipped schema v2 last quarter but some tenants are still on v1. Could that create missing fields?
sam: Yes. v2 renames actor.email -> actor.identity.email in some internal migrations. If the tenant's ingest path assumes actor.email it will show null. We must ensure our webhook shim includes backward-compatible aliases for at least one release cycle.
lex: I'll open a small rollout task to insert alias fields in the webhook payload for the next 2 weeks. For customers on S3 export, we'll document mapping table (v1 -> v2) and provide a tiny lambda to translate.
priya: For security/customer-facing validation steps to give them: 1) Confirm schema version header (X-Redwood-Audit-Version) 2) Send 5 sample events including an edge-case long-path and a permission-change with an actor that has only service-account subject_id 3) Verify HMAC and signature header reach their endpoint 4) For Splunk, capture raw HEC payload to check for truncation 5) For S3, confirm object size and metadata after upload
maya: Also note: if RBAC change caused actor to be a machine subject_id, they may need to map that to human identity in SIEM. We should offer a mapping CSV export for onboarding.
priya: Agreed — I'll prepare a template mapping CSV and include instructions.
lex: devops-bot, can you schedule a 30-min troubleshooting call with the customer for Thursday?
devops-bot: Scheduled: Audit delivery troubleshooting with acct-78 on Thu 2026-03-26 15:00 UTC. Invite sent to maya, priya, sam, lex.
maya: Perfect. After the call we'll run the contract test and either toggle the v2 aliases or update the customer's mapping. :thumbsup:
